purpose: Residual dynamics-model pilot: under dynamics shift, does a model built from 1M source rows plus a residual learned on the small target data predict held-out target transitions better than a model trained on target data alone? Model error only; no policy training, no simulator.
source: D4RL medium of the same robot from the transfer project (hopper-morph / walker2d-morph source_dataset), timeout rows dropped

models.S: source model only (trained on the source data, applied to the target unchanged)
models.T: trained on the target training blocks only
models.FT: source model weights and normalization, then fine-tuned on the target training blocks
models.RES: frozen source model plus a residual network trained on the target training blocks; prediction = source prediction + residual; the residual's last layer starts at zero

split.note: Each target trajectory is cut into consecutive blocks of 100 rows; blocks are assigned at random to test, validation (early stopping) and training. Train fractions use the first 25%, 50%, 100% of the training blocks in a fixed random order (nested).

rule.units: Errors are mean squared errors per dimension in units of the standard deviation of the full target training set of that repetition (state change for one-step state error, state for rollout error).
rule.primary: one-step next-state error on the held-out target test blocks, train fraction 1.0
rule.better: paired over the 5 repetitions (same split and seed): mean(error of the other model - error of RES) > 0 and > 2 * paired SE

decision.A: RES better than T and better than FT on both dense tasks: the residual direction is supported; next step would be a pilot that trains policies on data generated by the model (not started by this package).
decision.B: RES better than T on both dense tasks, but not better than FT on at least one: knowledge from the source dynamics helps, but the residual structure itself shows no advantage over fine-tuning; innovation 2 would be written as a source-pretrained target dynamics model with residual as one variant.
decision.C: otherwise: under dense shifts, the source data gives no reliable help for predicting target dynamics; the residual direction does not proceed to a policy pilot.

rule.sparse_tasks: reported as a reference only; they do not enter the decision
rule.secondary: rollout errors, near/far split by distance to the training blocks, reward error and the train-fraction sweep are descriptive
rule.caveat: A lower model error is necessary but not sufficient for a better policy.

failure_policy: A run killed by a signal is restarted from the beginning with the same seed in a new folder, at most 3 times. A Python error, NaN/Inf or failed audit stops new launches and is reported. Results are never used to decide a retry.
